steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Soak bread in enough warm water to cover in a small bowl; set aside.

Place beef in a large bowl. Add salsa, green onion, onion, Dijon mustard, garlic, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper to the bowl. Drain bread and add to beef. Mix by hand until well blended. Form into a loaf and place into the prepared loaf pan.
Bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour. Drain off excess fat and top with barbeque sauce. Return to the oven and bake for 15 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: A Firefighter’s Meatloaf
raw_recipe.description: Firefighters all across Canada can’t get enough of this Dijon mustard and salsa meatloaf recipe. Serve with baked beans and greens. Leftover sandwiches are great the next day.
raw_recipe.name: A Firefighter’s Meatloaf

review.reviewBody: We improvised on this, instead of bread, we used bread crumbs, 1 cup and a half, instead of barbecue sauce, we used ketchup, these were the ingredients we had on hand. Quick and easy, with pretty much all the ingredients in the fridge, this will not disappoint!

This was great! I made mini meatloaves and they are moist and flavorful! Important change that I will do again and again: when forming mink loaves, I enclosed a generous portion of smoked cheddar inside each loaf. Smoky yumminess was the result! Substitutions: 1/3 c. Dry bread crumbs instead of soaked bread, sweet Baby Rays BBQ sauce instead of ketchup on top, formed into 1/3 c. Mini meatloaves instead of making a whole loaf. Baked for 35 minutes.

Made according to recipe, using 1/2 cup plain breadcrumbs and an egg in place of the bread as another reviewer suggested. Could have used at least another 1/4 cup of breadcrumbs in order to make it hold together better. Taste was great! Husband and son loved it! I even had the good fortune to have some Diana's bbq sauce on hand. :) The onion, green onion and salsa are the real flavor players here!
I formed the mixture into a loaf in a 9" dish and just because i had it, laid partially cooked bacon slices over the unbaked meatloaf after brushing it with the bbq sauce. Brushed the bacon with bbq sauce, too and baked it about 40 minutes at 350 (it was a glass dish) till the bacon was crisp and the meatloaf registered 170 degrees. Really, really good! Will definitely make again, with or without added bacon!

We really enjoyed this. I used oatmeal and a little milk instead of bread and water. I also added an egg. Also way more than a tablespoon of bbq sauce. I used more onion and sauteed it with the garlic before adding. Everyone liked it a lot,especially the extra little kick from the salsa.

This was delicious. I can't eat wheat so I substituted 1/3 c of finely ground Kasha (toasted buckwheat, which is not wheat despite the name) and soaked it in 1/4 c of water. I had bought a meatloaf mix of beef and pork. I read through a bunch of reviews before making it. I took the advice to add an egg to hold it together. I didn't have green onions so I used 1 1/2 tablespoons of dried onions. I didn't have dijon mustard so I used spicy brown mustard and some horseradish sauce. I layered the BBQ sauce on the top. It was wonderful. My son and I ate FAR too much, but there was still plenty of leftovers for the fridge and freezer.

This was so good! I didn't use the soaked bread, just a 1/3 cup of plain bread crumbs, it held together just fine and was plenty juicy. If you put the bbq sauce on before it goes in the oven, it glazes better. :) yummm its a staple recipe now.

Since I always like trying something new and there are so very many meatloaf recipes I rarely do any of them more than once but this is one of the rare exceptions. Absolutely a winner! Only thing I did different was to use bread crumbs instead of bread and I did half ground beef and half ground pork. Loved how moist it was and how the flavors zinged with a bit of a kick. Did half the recipe and just the two of us nearly finished it. Great recipe. Leave it to the Canadians! Merci.

Very Good! Accidentally added the bbq sauce to the meat mixture, but half way through cooking time I topped the loaf with thinly sliced tomatoes and another drizzle of bbq sauce. Also, I soaked the bread in milk. Next time I might add more salsa to the mix for a bit more flavor or maybe a salsa with a little more heat than the one I used. Leftovers made a great sandwich!
With the addition of an egg for a binder, would give this recipe 5 stars...and changed the glaze from bbq sauce to 1/2 cup ketchup with 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar instead...yum

Loved this recipe!! Turned out with a ton of flavor and in my case some heat. I read some of the reviews and decided to go a little old school with using some homemade breadcrumbs and some egg. I didnt soak the bread. I will try that another time. I also ended up using pace picante hot which gave it the kick and I added bellpepper since I love it. Followed recipe otherwise and am eating it right now! Soo Good! Highly recommend recipe.

I really liked this meatloaf. I found the ingredients amounts sort of odd, esp. the onions though. I only had 1 lb of ground beef, so I could only make 1/2 recipe which was fine. I used Trader Joes 96% lean ground beef and their Kansas City BBQ sauce. I think the salsa was ChiChis brand, just a simple basic salsa. I finely minced the white onion, being as there wasn't much. I am glad I did, because after one hour of baking they were still oddly sort of crunchy. Unless, that was the salsa. I didn't have wheat bread, but I had parmesan bread sticks from Sam's club. For 1/2 the recipe I just used 1/2 of a bread stick. I didn't soak it in water. I just poured the salsa on top while I measured out the rest of the ingredients. I didn't have to do the draining part as my ground beef was so lean. I baked it in an oval shape in a foil lined pan I sprayed with cooking spray. It seemed done after an hour. I sprinkled it with a little garlic salt and topped with the bbq sauce. I probably added a bit more bbq sauce than suggested. I have never added that, that I can think of to a meatloaf, and liked that. I put it back in the oven for 5-7 minutes with the oven turned off. This was easy for a last minute meal. I would make it again. A nice change to salty seasoning packets. With the salsa and bbq sauce it is a little bit different though than the usual beef gravy type meatloaf. 1/2 the recipe, made as written here, yielded 4 good sized servings at about 220 calories each. ty

Do not waste your beef. This was the worst tasting meatloaf ever. I think it had to do with the soaked bread. Should have used my tomato sauce which is standard for meat loaf instead of the barbeque sauce. Will go back to my tried and true meatloaf.
I changed the bbq sauce with half a can of Manwich. And mixed in 1# of lean ground pork to the 2# of ground chuck. Very zippy , tangy flavor. Will make again!
It was delicious I took it to church brought home an empty dis everyone loved it. Very easy to make very moist.
I made this for a church dinner everyone loved it brought home an empty dish it’s delicious
I have made this recipe several times now and it always comes out delicious and gets rave reviews from people who don't normally like meatloaf. I don't make meatloaf any other way now.
I've tried this and it was moist and delicious! Best meatloaf recipe so far. I will try topping with ketchup next time.

My husband saw me making this and insisted he wasn't going to like it. When he smelled it cooking, he agreed to at least give it try. After tasting it, he insists that I make it again but to triple the recipe so he can have plenty of leftovers to take to work! He admitted that it was a lot better than his normal meatloaf recipe we use. (Which is big praise from him!)

I was a little nervous about this dish because it was so different from anything I'd done before. After reading a couple of reviews, I used 1 1/2 cups of Panko breadcrumbs and a green Salsa Verde (It was what I had.) It was ah-mazing! I always hold my breath when I make something new for my Sweet Hubby, (Pureblood Italian with a super chef mama to go with it!). But even he loved it. He refrained, he said, from saying it was better than his mother's recipe because he values his life. LOL Definitely keeping this one!
